text: I haven't asked any questions yet, so I am at question 1 of 10. When did you first notice this generalized rash on your newborn, and has it appeared anywhere else on the body besides the face?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum. While the maternal history of gonorrhea raises concern for sepsis, the acute onset of a generalized rash in a term infant born without complications is most characteristic of this benign self-limiting condition. I recommend a complete blood count and blood culture to definitively rule out septicemia before finalizing the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: CBC, Blood_Culture.
